children: UK education software provider's H1 revenue rose 7.1% yr/yr to £48.9 mln
Adjusted EBITDA was flat at £8.7 mln, with margin down due to adverse forex swing
Statutory profit after tax declined to £3.9 mln, mainly due to higher amortisation charges
Tribal expects FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA comfortably in line with market expectations
Market expectations for FY26: revenue £93.6m, adjusted EBITDA £17.0m, net cash £9.4m
Company sees significant Etio project tenders progressing in H2 2026 and into FY27
SUBSCRIPTION AND CLOUD GROWTH - Revenue growth was driven by increased adoption of subscription and cloud services, including successful migrations to HEFS and cloud offerings
ETIO CONTRACTS AND EFFICIENCY - Etio segment revenue increased, supported by government contracts and improved operational efficiency after a business review
ADVERSE FOREX SWING - Adjusted EBITDA margin declined due to a £0.9m adverse forex swing from intercompany trading balances
HIGHER AMORTISATION CHARGES - Statutory profit after tax declined, mainly due to higher amortisation, including a one-off charge from realigning product go-live dates
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "strong buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 2 "strong buy" or "buy", no "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the professional & business education peer group is "buy."
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Tribal Group PLC is GBp93.50, about 48.4% above its September 2 closing price of GBp63.00
The stock recently traded at 14 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 15 three months ago
